question: When I put my 2021 Jetta in reverse, sometimes the screen just goes black or the whole display locks up and I can’t see behind me. Is there a recall for this?
reference_answer: Yes, 20V716000: the rear-view camera can fail when the car is started, leaving a black or frozen screen. Dealers update the infotainment software free of charge.
notes: Symptom only; camera and software not named.

question: I’ve been hearing a metallic scraping noise from the front wheels of my 2020 Tesla Model 3. Could it be a recall issue?
reference_answer: Yes, 21V387000: brake caliper bolts may be loose, allowing the caliper to separate and contact the wheel rim. Tesla Service will inspect and tighten or replace the caliper bolts free of charge.
notes: Describes symptom (metallic scraping) without naming brakes or calipers.

question: My 2019 RAV4 feels unstable at highway speeds and the front end clunks over bumps. Has Toyota recalled anything related to this?
reference_answer: Yes, 20V286000: the front lower suspension arms may have cracks which could cause them to break. Dealers will replace both front lower suspension arms free of charge.
notes: Symptom description matches suspension recall but does not name suspension.

question: I read online that some Honda CR-Vs had a problem where the rear of the car could basically fall apart. Is my 2020 CR-V affected?
reference_answer: Yes, 19V865000: the rear subframe bolts were improperly manufactured and may loosen, allowing the rear subframe to separate. Dealers will inspect and retorque or replace the bolts free of charge.
notes: Paraphrased from internet rumor style; subframe not named directly.

question: The steering on my 2021 F-150 suddenly got really stiff and hard to turn. The dealer said not to drive it. What recall is this?
reference_answer: This is recall 21V407000: the steering gear may have internal damage resulting in difficulty steering or inability to rotate the steering wheel. Vehicles will be towed in for service and dealers will replace the steering gear free of charge.
notes: Owner describes symptom and dealer advice; matches the do-not-drive recall.

question: I just bought a used 2022 Hyundai Tucson. Are there any recalls I should know about?
reference_answer: Yes, there are 3 recalls: 21V938000 (ICU software may cause inoperative headlights/taillights), 23V038000 (roof moldings may detach), and 25V893000 (tow hitch wiring may short circuit causing fire risk).
notes: Used car buyer asking about all recalls.

question: I heard the Chevy Bolt had a huge battery fire recall. Is my 2020 Bolt EV part of that?
reference_answer: Yes, 21V650000: the high voltage battery could catch fire when charged to full or nearly full capacity. GM will replace the battery modules free of charge.
notes: Owner heard about battery fire; 21V650000 is the main battery fire recall.

question: My 2020 Subaru Outback jerks when shifting and sometimes loses power while driving. Is this a known problem?
reference_answer: Yes, recalls 21V955000 and 22V485000: a programming error in the Transmission Control Unit may allow the clutch to engage before the drive chain is properly secured. The chain may slip and break, causing loss of drive power. Dealers will reprogram the TCU and inspect for damage free of charge.
notes: Symptom matches both transmission recalls; either is acceptable.

question: I have a 2022 Kia Sorento with a tow hitch installed. My neighbor said there was a fire recall. Should I be worried?
reference_answer: Yes, 22V703000: vehicles equipped with a tow hitch harness may have a wiring issue that can cause a fire. Owners are advised to park outside and away from structures. Dealers will inspect and replace the fuse and/or tow hitch harness module free of charge.
notes: Owner knows about tow hitch and fire risk from neighbor.

question: The wheels on my 2021 Nissan Rogue vibrate badly even after balancing. The shop said the lug nuts might be wrong. Is there a recall?
reference_answer: Yes, 21V186000: incorrect wheel nuts may have been installed which may loosen and cause wheel vibration. Dealers will inspect and replace any incorrect wheel nuts free of charge.
notes: Owner describes vibration symptom; mechanic hint about lug nuts.

question: Are there any airbag recalls on the 2020 BMW X3? I want to make sure my passenger side is safe.
reference_answer: Yes, there are two airbag-related recalls: 20V152000 (instrument panel casing may not be properly bonded, causing fragments to strike occupants when airbag deploys) and 20V164000 (air bags and seat belt pretensioners may deploy improperly). Dealers will replace parts free of charge.
notes: Asks specifically about airbags; either airbag recall is acceptable.

question: I noticed the driver seat belt in my 2021 Model Y feels loose where it connects to the pillar. Is this something Tesla recalled?
reference_answer: Yes, 21V389000: one or both fasteners securing the front seat shoulder belt to the B-pillar may not be properly attached. Tesla Service will inspect and repair both fasteners if necessary free of charge.
notes: Describes exact symptom of loose B-pillar connection.

question: The steering in my 2021 Jeep Grand Cherokee L makes a clunking sound and feels like it could disconnect. Has Jeep issued a recall?
reference_answer: Yes, 23V352000: an incorrectly assembled steering column intermediate shaft may disconnect from the steering gear, causing a loss of steering control. Dealers will inspect and replace the intermediate shaft and assembly parts as necessary free of charge.
notes: Question says Grand Cherokee L but model is GRAND CHEROKEE; 23V352000 covers both per DB.

question: I own a 2020 Dodge Charger and I’m worried about the side curtain airbags. I heard some can explode and send metal fragments. Is my car affected?
reference_answer: Yes, 24V198000: the right and left side curtain air bag inflators may rupture due to a manufacturing defect, resulting in sharp metal fragments striking occupants. Dealers will replace both side curtain air bags free of charge.
notes: Specific concern about inflator rupture.

question: My 2020 Toyota Camry overheated and the dealer says the engine block might have a defect. Is there a recall for this?
reference_answer: Yes, 20V064000: certain 2.5L 4-cylinder engines may have a manufacturing defect causing coolant leaks. The engine can overheat and stall. Dealers will inspect and replace the engine including the engine block as necessary free of charge.
notes: Owner describes overheating symptom matching engine recall.

question: Steering my 2022 Honda Civic has gotten noticeably harder lately, especially at low speeds in parking lots. Could this be a recall?
reference_answer: Yes, 24V744000: the worm gear spring in the electric power steering may cause difficulty steering. Dealers will replace the worm gear spring and redistribute or add grease as necessary free of charge.
notes: 23V704000 only applies to vehicles with a prior service repair; 24V744000 is the general steering recall.

question: I smell gas near the engine of my 2021 Hyundai Sonata with the turbo engine. Should I be concerned about a recall?
reference_answer: Yes, 21V524000: fuel may leak at the pipe connection between the high-pressure fuel pump and fuel rail on 2.5L turbocharged engines. Dealers will inspect and tighten or replace the fuel pipe free of charge.
notes: Smell of gas near engine matches the turbo fuel leak recall.

question: The airbag warning light keeps coming on in my 2021 Chevy Silverado 1500. I’m worried the driver airbag won’t work. Is there a recall?
reference_answer: Yes, 21V495000: the front driver's side air bag module may be missing metal tabs that secure the plastic air bag cover, which may prevent proper deployment. Dealers will inspect and replace if necessary free of charge.
notes: Warning light symptom; specific airbag defect matches.

question: There’s a strong fuel smell coming from under the hood of my 2021 Ford Escape with the 1.5L engine. I’m afraid of a fire. Any recalls?
reference_answer: Yes, 22V859000: a fuel injector may crack and leak fuel inside the engine compartment, increasing fire risk. Dealers will update the engine control software and install a drain tube free of charge.
notes: Fuel smell + fire concern matches the fuel injector cracking recall.

question: The front bumper on my 2020 Toyota Highlander is sagging and looks like it might come off. Is this a known defect?
reference_answer: Yes, 23V720000: minor impact to the front lower bumper cover can cause it to detach and become a road hazard. Dealers will repair or replace the upper and lower front bumper covers as necessary free of charge.
notes: Describes bumper detachment symptom.

question: I heard Kia Tellurides can catch fire because of the power seats. Is my 2020 affected and should I park outside?
reference_answer: Yes, recalls 24V407000 and 26V430000: the front power seat motor may overheat due to a stuck slide knob, which can cause a fire. Owners are advised to park outside and away from structures. Dealers will install parts free of charge.
notes: Owner already knows about fire risk and parking advice.

question: My 2021 GMC Sierra 1500 with the 6.2 is burning through oil way too fast. Is there a recall for engine problems?
reference_answer: Yes, 25V274000: certain vehicles with the 6.2L V8 may have connecting rod and crankshaft manufacturing defects that can lead to engine damage and failure. Dealers will inspect and as necessary repair or replace the engine free of charge.
notes: Oil consumption symptom; 25V274000 is the 6.2L V8 engine recall.

question: I pressed the brake pedal on my 2021 Ram 1500 and it went all the way to the floor with almost no resistance. Is this a recall?
reference_answer: Yes, 21V037000: certain vehicles were built without the retaining clip that secures the master cylinder push rod to the brake pedal, which can cause the brake pedal to separate. Owners are advised not to drive until repaired. Dealers will inspect and install the push rod retaining clip free of charge.
notes: Brake pedal going to floor matches the missing retaining clip recall.

question: Our 2021 Chrysler Pacifica hybrid shuts off unexpectedly while driving. Is there a recall for this?
reference_answer: Yes, 23V010000: an internal transmission wiring connector may short circuit, resulting in an unexpected engine shutdown and loss of drive power. Dealers will update the Power Inverter Module software free of charge.
notes: 23V010000 covers PACIFICA (not PACIFICA PLUG-IN HYBRID) per recall_vehicles. Unexpected shutdown matches the connector short-circuit defect.

question: My 2020 Nissan Altima’s engine started making a knocking sound and the check engine light came on. Could this be related to a recall?
reference_answer: Yes, 25V437000: certain vehicles with variable compression turbo engines may have bearing failures causing engine failure and potential fire risk. Dealers will reprogram the engine control module software free of charge.
notes: Engine knocking matches the engine bearing failure recall.

question: I feel a wobble from the rear end of my 2021 Audi Q5 at highway speed. Has Audi recalled anything for the rear suspension?
reference_answer: Yes, 21V295000: the rear axle assembly may not have been properly manufactured. Dealers will replace the rear axle assembly free of charge.
notes: Rear wobble symptom matches rear axle recall.

notes: Spongy brake pedal matches the VSA modulator brake fluid leak recall.
